arguments.name: country
arguments.description: Country name as the sources spell it, e.g. Sudan

arguments.name: days
arguments.description: Length of each comparison window in days

prompts.name: conflict-trend
prompts.title: Conflict trend in one country against the previous period
prompts.question: How has organized violence in {country} changed over the last {days} days, and is it more or less intense than the {days} days before that?

steps.purpose: UCDP events of all three types (state-based, non-state and one-sided; see type_of_violence_label) for every country. It needs UCDP_ACCESS_TOKEN: without it, or when the API refuses it, the tool returns an error with reason ucdp_unconfigured or ucdp_fetch_failed, which is missing data, not zero events. It has no country filter, so keep the events in {country} yourself, split them at {days} days ago by date_start, and say that you filtered. limit is the page size and every page is requested, so it does not cap the result. When a page could not be fetched the result carries reason ucdp_partial and pages_failed: its count and fatalities are then lower bounds, so say the list is incomplete

ACLED events in {country} over both windows. It needs ACLED_EMAIL and ACLED_PASSWORD; without them it returns an error naming them. limit caps the result: a count equal to the limit means the list may have been cut off, so say so or call again with a higher limit

protests and riots in {country} (also ACLED, same credentials), kept apart from armed violence. Nearby duplicates are merged: count plus deduplicated is what was fetched, and when that equals the limit the list may have been cut off

limits: Event datasets are revised and arrive late, so the most recent days are the least complete. A quiet final week is not proof of calm.

UCDP is read from one pinned GED release (gedevents/25.1), which holds events only up to its own cutoff. The tool states neither that cutoff nor a marker when your window lies after it: it drops the older events and returns count 0. Check the latest date_start UCDP returned; when count is 0, or the newest event is well before the window ends, UCDP has no data for that span, which is missing data, not zero events.
Count events and fatalities separately: fewer events with more deaths is not de-escalation.
ACLED and UCDP define an event differently. Compare each source with itself across the two windows, never one source's count against the other's.

prompts.name: hotspot-escalation
prompts.title: Which hotspots are escalating and why
prompts.question: Which of the built-in hotspots score highest for escalation right now, and which measured component drives each score?

steps.purpose: scores and their components for the 22 hotspots
foreign military aircraft concentrations against baseline
military aircraft presence by theater

limits: Escalation scores are weighted heuristics against fixed baselines, renormalized over the components actually measured. They are not probabilities of war. List the unavailable_components.

The escalation score's military component is 0 at every hotspot whatever the aircraft data, during a flight outage too, and unavailable_components does not list it: take military activity from intel_military_surge and intel_theater_posture instead.

Aircraft tracking sees only aircraft that broadcast a position, and many military flights do not, so counts are a floor. A theater that no flight source answered for is listed in intel_theater_posture's unavailable_theaters, and its regions in intel_military_surge's unchecked_regions: its count is unknown, not zero. With no source answering anywhere, both tools return an error.

prompts.name: market-risk-snapshot
prompts.title: Cross-asset risk picture today
prompts.question: What does the current risk picture look like across equities, volatility, the dollar, rates and crypto?

steps.purpose: Fear and Greed, VIX, DXY, gold, 10-year yield, BTC dominance
which US equity sectors are leading and lagging
curve shape and spreads
the composite score and the inputs it weighs
keyless liquidity readings (Fed balance sheet, Treasury General Account, reverse repo, net liquidity, money supply), each with its units and observation date
only if liquidity matters to the answer: the weekly US net liquidity series behind the board's row, with its formula

limits: Report current readings and their recent change only. Quote the composite score next to its inputs, since it is a weighted summary of them.

prompts.name: yield-curve-check
prompts.title: Is the Treasury curve inverted, and by how much
prompts.question: Is the US Treasury yield curve inverted today, by how much, and how has the 10-year minus 2-year spread moved recently?

steps.purpose: maturities, the 2s10s and 3m10y spreads and the inversion flag
the spread's recent daily history (needs FRED_API_KEY)
the policy rate the short end is anchored to
only if FRED_API_KEY is not set: loads the T10Y2Y history from FRED's keyless graph CSV into the history store (it stores no unit for this series; a failed fetch is an error capture)
only after that backfill: the stored T10Y2Y observations with their observed_at dates

limits: Spreads are in percentage points. A move from 0.10 to 0.30 is 0.20 points, not a 200 percent rise.

Without FRED_API_KEY the curve falls back to four Yahoo maturities (3M, 5Y, 10Y, 30Y) with no observation dates, so spread_2s10s comes back null. Say so; do not swap in another spread without saying which.
An inverted curve describes today's yields. It is not a recession forecast.

prompts.name: central-bank-compare
prompts.title: Where major central bank policy rates stand
prompts.question: Where do the Federal Reserve, ECB and Bank of England policy rates stand now, how has the US federal funds rate moved recently, and what did the other major central banks last set, as of the dates on record?

steps.purpose: rates for 15 central banks; each entry carries its source (fred or curated) and as_of date
the daily effective federal funds rate history (needs FRED_API_KEY)
the major currency cross rates: how they sit against each other today
only if FRED_API_KEY is not set: loads the effective federal funds rate history from FRED's keyless graph CSV into the history store (a failed fetch is an error capture)
only after that backfill: the stored observations of that rate with their observed_at dates

limits: Only the Fed, ECB and BoE rates can be live, read from FRED when FRED_API_KEY is set (source fred). The other twelve come from a hand-kept table dated 2024-11 to 2025-02 (source curated): report them as stale, with their as_of dates, never as current.
fred_available only says that FRED_API_KEY is set, not that FRED answered. A curated Fed, ECB or BoE entry means the FRED read failed or the key is missing.

The live Fed figure is the effective rate (DFF) and the live BoE figure is SONIA, an overnight market rate that tracks Bank Rate; the curated Fed entry is the upper bound of the target range. Do not read a gap between a live and a curated figure as a policy change.
Rate changes are in percentage points or basis points (one point is 100 basis points), not percent of the rate.

arguments.name: symbol
arguments.description: Quote currency, ISO code such as EUR

prompts.name: fx-move
prompts.title: A currency pair's move and the coverage around it
prompts.question: How has {symbol} moved against {base} over the last {days} days, and what news coverage ran alongside the largest daily moves?

steps.purpose: daily ECB reference rates. Each rate is units of {symbol} per 1 {base}, and trend.change_pct is the change in that number: a positive change means one {base} buys more {symbol}, so {symbol} weakened against {base}. Say which way you quote the move
where the pair sits among the majors today

args.what: the currency's name, such as yen or euro

steps.purpose: recent articles about the currency. The tool has no date parameter and searches GDELT's default window, so keep the articles whose seendate falls on or just after the dates of the largest moves, and say how many matched

limits: ECB reference rates are published once per business day. A weekend or holiday has no observation, which is not a zero change.
An empty rates list with a null trend means the fetch failed, not that the currency was flat.
News published alongside a move is context. Timing alone does not show that the news caused the move.

prompts.name: company-events
prompts.title: A company's recent disclosures and results
prompts.question: What material events has {ticker} disclosed recently, and how did its reported results compare with estimates?

steps.purpose: quote, sector and recent news
recent 10-K, 10-Q and 8-K filings
actual against estimated earnings

companies named in recent news story clusters with the stock's move on the story's session against a benchmark. If {ticker} is not listed, no recent cluster was mapped to it, which is not the same as no news

limits: A filing date is when the company filed, not when the event happened; give both when the filing states the event date.
No buy, sell or hold view: describe what was disclosed.

prompts.name: energy-pressure
prompts.title: Energy prices from futures to the pump
prompts.question: Are energy prices rising for producers and for consumers, and is any chokepoint exposure relevant to the move?

steps.purpose: crude oil and natural gas futures
EIA crude and gas prices (needs EIA_API_KEY)
AAA US retail gasoline and diesel averages
oil flows through the major chokepoints

limits: Futures, wholesale and retail pump prices are different measures with different dates. Never join them into one series.
Chokepoint oil flows are curated reference values, not live tanker counts.

prompts.name: crypto-structure
prompts.title: Crypto market structure today
prompts.question: What is the state of the crypto market today: prices, stablecoin pegs, spot ETF trading and Bitcoin's trend indicators?

steps.purpose: prices and market caps of the largest coins
whether the major stablecoins hold their peg
Bitcoin spot ETF prices and trading volume
moving averages, Mayer Multiple and distance from the highest daily price of the last 200 days (ath_in_period, not the all-time high)

limits: intel_etf_flows reports prices and trading volume, not creations or redemptions. Volume is not net flow.
Technical indicators summarize past prices; they do not predict the next move.

prompts.name: earthquake-exposure
prompts.title: Recent strong earthquakes near people
prompts.question: Which earthquakes of magnitude {min_magnitude} or more in the last {hours} hours struck near large populations, and did any raise a disaster alert?

steps.purpose: the earthquakes, newest first and at most 50 by default, so a count of 50 means older ones may have been cut off; call again with a higher limit to check

major cities within radius_km (default 200) of recent events. It ignores the magnitude and hours above: it fetches its own list of M4.5 and larger quakes from the last 48 hours, at most 50, and names only the nearest of them for each city, so a city's event_detail ("M<magnitude> <place>") can name a smaller aftershock while a step-1 event is also within reach. Before dropping a city, compare its lat and lon with each step-1 event and keep it if any lies within radius_km; check events_analyzed: 0 can mean its fetch failed
the GDACS alert level of the same events

limits: Exposure knows only 105 major cities, each with at least 1.4 million people. It is not a casualty estimate and misses everyone outside those cities.
Magnitudes and locations are revised in the first hours after an event; say when you read them.

arguments.name: us_area
arguments.description: Two-letter US state code, e.g. TX

prompts.name: severe-weather
prompts.title: Severe weather warnings in the covered regions
prompts.question: What severe weather warnings are active in {us_area} and in {europe_country}, and are any tropical cyclones active?

steps.purpose: US National Weather Service alerts
European warnings, one country per call; without country it lists the countries it covers
Atlantic and eastern and central Pacific storms from the National Hurricane Center
western Pacific, Indian Ocean and Southern Hemisphere storms from JTWC

limits: NWS covers the US and Meteoalarm covers its participating European countries only. No alert outside those areas says nothing about the weather there.
NHC and JTWC cover different basins and can label the same storm differently. Match storms by position and time before counting.

arguments.name: region
arguments.description: FIRMS region: north_america, south_america, europe, africa, middle_east, south_asia, east_asia, southeast_asia or oceania

prompts.name: wildfire-situation
prompts.title: Wildfire activity and the conditions around it
prompts.question: How active are wildfires in {region} now, and are temperatures or rainfall abnormal there?

steps.purpose: satellite fire detections (needs NASA_FIRMS_API_KEY)
named fires NASA EONET tracks
temperature and precipitation against the prior year

limits: FIRMS detections are satellite heat signatures, not mapped fire perimeters; one large fire produces many detections.

Without NASA_FIRMS_API_KEY the fire tool returns an error. With a key set, a region FIRMS did not answer is named in failed_regions and carries its own error (its count of 0 is not a measurement), and every region failing is an error. Report either as missing data, not zero fires.
Climate anomalies are measured against the prior year, not a long-term normal.

prompts.name: space-weather-impact
prompts.title: Space weather and coincident outages
prompts.question: How strong is current geomagnetic and solar activity, and are internet or cloud outages being reported at the same time?

steps.purpose: Kp index, flare class, solar wind and SWPC alerts
internet outages reported over the last 7 days
active incidents at the major cloud providers

limits: An outage at the same time as a storm does not show the storm caused it; most outages have local causes.
An empty outage list can mean that both outage sources failed; the tool does not always say so.
Kp runs 0 to 9 on a quasi-logarithmic scale: Kp 8 is far more than twice Kp 4.

arguments.name: role
arguments.description: origin (its people abroad, plus IDPs) or host (people it hosts)

prompts.name: displacement-history
prompts.title: A country's displacement record since 1951
prompts.question: How has displacement linked to {country} as {role} changed since records began, and which years saw the largest waves?

steps.purpose: the yearly record
the latest year's largest corridors out of {country}; for the host view call it with destination {country} instead
UNHCR's global displacement totals, for context

args.what: the country as CBP names it, in capitals, e.g. MEXICO

steps.purpose: only for the origin view: US CBP encounters per month of {country} citizens, a flow of events (not people, not a stock) that never adds to the displacement figures above

limits: UNHCR figures are year-end stocks (people displaced at the end of each year), not arrivals during the year. A change between two years is a net change in the stock.
UNHCR revises past years. Say which reporting year you used.

prompts.name: migration-surges
prompts.title: The largest year-over-year displacement changes
prompts.question: Which origins and corridors had the largest year-over-year change in displacement in {year}, and how does that compare with net migration from all causes?

steps.purpose: the largest increases and decreases against the year before
World Bank net migration for the leading countries
HDX crisis datasets for the leading origins
only if the question turns to arrivals in the US: CBP encounters per month with same-month prior-year change, a flow of events, not a stock
only if the question turns to arrivals in the UK: Home Office small boat crossings with year to date against last year, a flow of arrivals, not a stock

limits: World Bank net migration counts every reason, work included; UNHCR counts forcibly displaced people. Show them side by side and never add them together.
The mass, major and notable levels are the tool's stated thresholds, not official designations.

arguments.name: region
arguments.description: global, conus, north_america, europe, middle_east or east_asia

prompts.name: airspace-anomaly
prompts.title: Unusual business jet or military air activity
prompts.question: Is {cohort} air activity over {region} unusual for this time of the week, and if so, where did the extra aircraft come from?

steps.purpose: the current picture; this call also builds the tracked cohort
the latest half-hour against the same slot on earlier weeks
only if step 2 flags an excess: where the extra departures came from
for the military cohort, a second source of positions

limits: ADS-B shows only aircraft whose transponders volunteer receivers pick up; many military and some private aircraft do not broadcast a usable position, so counts are a floor.

When intel_military_flights reports source none, no flight source answered: it carries error, degraded and reason military_flights_unavailable, and its empty aircraft list is unknown, not an empty sky.
An anomaly is a deviation from the same slot on earlier weeks. It is not evidence of anyone's intent.
The anomaly check needs a learned cohort; a fresh install reports that gap first.

prompts.name: airport-disruption
prompts.title: US airport delays and their likely weather context
prompts.question: Which major US airports have delays now, and is severe weather active near them?

steps.purpose: FAA delays at 20 major US airports
the airborne traffic snapshot for scale
NWS alerts for the states of the delayed airports

limits: FAA data covers major US airports only.
The airborne total is a snapshot of aircraft OpenSky receives, not a count of all flights.

prompts.name: cyber-landscape
prompts.title: Current cyber threat landscape
prompts.question: What does the current cyber threat picture look like: newly known-exploited vulnerabilities, active malware infrastructure, and which threat actors are in the headlines?

steps.purpose: Feodo, CISA KEV, SANS and URLhaus indicators
CVE and APT names rising in headlines against baseline
CVEs, APT groups and organizations in recent headlines

limits: Feeds list reported indicators and known-exploited vulnerabilities. A listing is not attribution and does not show that any particular organization was hit.
Keyword spikes measure mentions in headlines, not attack volume.

arguments.name: resource
arguments.description: An ASN or prefix to check, e.g. AS3333

prompts.name: internet-disruption
prompts.title: Internet disruption in one country
prompts.question: Is internet connectivity in {country} disrupted now, and could a cable corridor failure explain it?

steps.purpose: outages over the last 7 days; keep those in {country}
routing visibility for that network
the condition of the six cable corridors
which countries depend on an at-risk corridor

limits: An empty outage list, an all-clear corridor reading or zero cable warnings can each be a failed fetch: when the warning feed is down every corridor reads clear. Check failing_sources in intel://guide/source-health before calling {country} connected: it lists every source whose last call failed, even before its circuit breaker opens.
Cascade analysis is a simulation over curated cable dependencies, not a measurement of a real outage.
BGP status checks one ASN or prefix at a time; it is not a global hijack detector.

prompts.name: cloud-incidents
prompts.title: Cloud provider incidents and the regions involved
prompts.question: Which cloud providers report active incidents, and which of their regions are involved?

steps.purpose: active incidents at AWS, Azure, GCP, Cloudflare and GitHub
where the named cloud regions are

limits: Status pages are published by the providers themselves and can lag or understate an incident.

prompts.name: maritime-chokepoints
prompts.title: Pressure on maritime chokepoints
prompts.question: Are navigational warnings building at the strategic waterways, and is shipping stress rising in markets?

steps.purpose: a warning-based status for the nine strategic waterways
the warning texts behind the status
what share of oil and trade each chokepoint carries
a stress score from shipping-linked ETF and equity prices

limits: The vessel snapshot counts navigational warnings, not ships. A warning counts at a waterway only when a position its text states lies within 300 km of the waterway's reference point (matching_rule states the rule).
A naval warning that states no readable position counts at no waterway and changes no status. It is listed in unplaced_naval_warnings with the reason: read those before calling any waterway clear.

A waterway status of unknown means the warning feed was unavailable (error, degraded and reason say why), not a quiet sea. A status of stale means the feed's newest warning is older than stale_after_days: the counts describe the feed's last update (status_as_of), not today. Check feed_stale and newest_issue_date before calling any status current.

The navarea filter of intel_nav_warnings takes NGA area codes (4, 12, A, P, C), their series names, or IV and XII for 4 and 12. Other NAVAREAs arrive inside the A, P and C series, and asking for one returns an error with reason navarea_not_carried, not a count of 0.
The shipping stress score is a market proxy, not a freight rate.

prompts.name: aoi-watch-setup
prompts.title: Start watching an area of interest
prompts.question: Set up a watch on {name} (centre {lat}, {lon}, radius {radius_km} km): what is inside it now, and what should later checks compare against?

steps.purpose: saves the area
only if a circle does not fit the area (a border region or a strait): define it under another name as a polygon of [lat, lon] vertices, and use that name in the steps below

args.what: the total width in km, 1 to 500

steps.purpose: only if the area is a route (a shipping lane or cable run): define it under another name as a corridor of waypoints with a width, and use that name in the steps below
the cited picture inside {name} today
the first change detection call records a baseline for {name}

limits: The first change check records a baseline and claims nothing entered or left.

A domain that fails is listed in data_gaps and left out of the diff; a wildfire region FIRMS did not answer is listed as partial coverage. Never read a failed domain as everything leaving. A whole domain departing at once with no data_gaps entry is still unconfirmed: check failing_sources in intel://guide/source-health and say it could not be confirmed.
Each intel_aoi_changes call compares with the snapshot saved by the call before it (yours or a collector AOI sweep) and then replaces that snapshot.

prompts.name: aoi-review
prompts.title: What changed in a watched area
prompts.question: What entered or left {name} since the last snapshot, and is the area escalating?

steps.purpose: confirm {name} is among the defined areas of interest and see its shape
new, departed and unchanged items since the previous snapshot, and previous_taken_at, when that snapshot was saved
the escalation score and its components for {name}
cited detail behind any change worth reporting
only if asked about every watched area: the change sweep across all defined AOIs in one call. It advances each AOI's snapshot as step 2 does, so never run both for {name}

limits: Changes are relative to the previous snapshot, whenever it was saved; give previous_taken_at.
Every intel_aoi_changes call saves a new snapshot. Call it once: a retried call compares with the snapshot the first call just saved and reports that nothing changed.

A domain that fails, earthquakes and wildfires included, is listed in data_gaps and left out of the changes; a wildfire region FIRMS did not answer is listed as partial coverage. A whole domain departing at once with no data_gaps entry is still unconfirmed: check failing_sources in intel://guide/source-health and report it as unconfirmed.
News for an AOI is found by place name near its centre, so a nearby place with the same name can leak in.

prompts.name: story-breadth
prompts.title: How widely a story is covered and how that changed
prompts.question: How much coverage has {topic} received, how has that changed over time, and which story clusters carry it?

steps.purpose: coverage volume over time
the articles themselves
the clusters of related stories in the RSS set
the latest items from the RSS feeds
stories carried by at least three distinct outlets in the RSS feeds over the last 24 hours, ranked by outlet count: breadth across outlets
situations between and inside countries ranked by how many RSS headlines cover them

args.what: the country the story is about

steps.purpose: only if the story is about one country or a pair: per-day GDELT article counts for it, where a day GDELT did not return is null and listed in data_gaps

limits: Report the timelinevol series as GDELT returns it and compare it with itself over time. Do not state a unit for it or call it an article count.
Coverage volume measures attention, not truth or importance.
The RSS set is a fixed list of feeds. A story missing there may still be covered elsewhere.

arguments.name: country
arguments.description: ISO alpha-3 country code, e.g. FRA

prompts.name: election-watch
prompts.title: Upcoming elections and the signals around them
prompts.question: Which elections are coming up in {country}, and what do current signals show around them?

steps.purpose: entries from a hand-kept election table of 18 rows dated 2025-01 to 2029-04, each with a status and a proximity risk

economy, sanctions, news and conflict context. It knows only the 50 countries in its own table and returns an error for others. Its sanctions section lists sanctions-list entries whose remarks name the country, which is not an exposure screen; match_count null means the sanctions list could not be read, not zero matches
discussion velocity on the tracked subreddits
the 20 active Polymarket questions with the most 24-hour volume. It has no topic filter, so most will be about other things: keep any about this election and say so if there are none
Kalshi open markets in its Elections category, ranked by volume; keep only those about this election
the same Elections markets on Kalshi and Polymarket side by side with the price gap; match_confidence ranks pairs and is not a probability

limits: The calendar is a fixed table, not a feed. An empty list means the country is not in it, not that no election is due; say the calendar does not cover it.
Entries with status past have already happened. Leave them out of upcoming elections: their proximity risk scores the days after an election like the days before it.
The country filter also matches part of a country name (RUS returns Belarus), so keep only entries whose iso3 is the code you asked for.
Proximity risk rises as an election nears; it is a stated heuristic, not a forecast of unrest or of the result.
Reddit and prediction markets reflect their own participants, not the electorate.

prompts.name: sanctions-screen
prompts.title: Search the OFAC sanctions list for a name
prompts.question: Does {query} appear on the US Treasury OFAC SDN list, and under which programs?

steps.purpose: name matches on the SDN sanctions list

args.what: the matched company's name or ticker

steps.purpose: only if a match is a listed company: who it is

limits: If total_entities is 0, the list could not be read. That is a failed search, not a clean result. Otherwise total_entities counts the entries read before the search stopped, not the size of the list.
Only the primary name of each entry is searched, not its aliases, so a listed party under another spelling will not match.
Results stop at the limit (default 50): a count equal to the limit means more names may have matched, so search again with a higher limit before saying how many did.
Matching is by substring on names. A name match is not an identity match, and this is not a compliance screening service. Never answer that a party is not sanctioned.
The SDN list changes. Say when you searched.

prompts.name: disease-watch
prompts.title: Disease outbreak reports
prompts.question: Which disease outbreaks are being reported now, and which involve high-concern pathogens?

steps.purpose: WHO, ProMED and CIDRAP outbreak reports
crisis datasets for the affected countries
recent news coverage, for context only

limits: Outbreak reports arrive after cases occur and case counts are revised. Give each report's date.
Reporting is uneven across countries. Fewer reports does not mean fewer cases.

arguments.name: hours
arguments.description: How far back to search, in hours

prompts.name: history-recall
prompts.title: What the stored history says about a topic
prompts.question: What has this server stored about {topic} over the last {hours} hours, and has anything similar been recorded before?

steps.purpose: what is stored per category in your window, with the earliest timestamp inside that window
the same over ten years: its earliest timestamps show when storage began for each domain
the stored entries closest in wording to the topic
the stored entries in time order for the matching domain

args.what: the text of the strongest match from step 3

steps.purpose: earlier stored events similar to the strongest match
the numeric series the history store holds (a separate store from the vector store), with observed_at, published_at and collected_at for each
the collector's run log per source: last success, consecutive failures and whether it is overdue, which says how complete that history is

limits: History exists only for what the collector stored while it was running. The earliest timestamp in step 1 is only the earliest inside your window; use step 2 before calling anything the first or the largest.
Semantic search ranks by similarity of wording. A high score is not a factual match.
If the vector store is not available these tools return an error; say that history could not be read.

arguments.name: country
arguments.description: ISO alpha-3 country code, e.g. UKR

prompts.name: country-overview
prompts.title: One country across economy, stability and markets
prompts.question: What is the current picture in {country} across economy, stability, active signals and its stock market?

steps.purpose: economy, elections, sanctions, news and conflict. It knows only the 50 countries in its own table and returns an error for others. Its sanctions section lists sanctions-list entries whose remarks name the country, which is not an exposure screen; match_count null means the sanctions list could not be read, not zero matches

the index with its four components. It takes 50 ISO alpha-3 codes and returns an error listing them for any other. Each input it could not obtain is named in data_gaps and its component is null; index_is_lower_bound then means the total counts the missing parts as zero
active signals; this tool takes the country's name, not its code
its main stock index; countries without a mapped index return an error that lists the ones covered

limits: The instability index is a weighted composite with country multipliers. Quote its components, not only the total. Its ucdp_floor comes from a static baseline table, not from current UCDP data: a total at the floor says nothing about this month.
World Bank figures in the dossier are annual and often a year or more old. Give the year of each.

The dossier's elections section reads a hand-kept election table: empty means the country is not covered, not that no vote is due, and its match on part of a name can add another country's election, so keep only entries whose iso3 is {country}.

commonLimits: A tool that returns an error, a note or a data_gaps entry has told you what is missing: report it as missing. Missing data is never zero, calm or peace.

Many tools do not mark a failure. When every upstream request fails they return an empty list, a zero count, a neutral score, a LOW risk label, an all-clear status or a false flag. Read an empty list or a zero as nothing returned, not nothing happened, and confirm with a second tool before calling a place quiet.
Give each figure the date it describes (the observation date) as well as when it was fetched; they are often different. If a tool gives no observation date, say so.
Describe what the data show. This server does not forecast prices, give trading advice or prove causation.
answerShape: Answer with: the place, period and measure you used; each number with its unit (or say the source states none) and date; the comparison you were asked for; every data gap; and one line on what this data cannot tell.
guideIntro:
# World Intelligence MCP: research guide

This server answers questions about the world with live public data:
markets, conflict, hazards, migration, aviation, cyber, infrastructure,
news and more. This guide is generated from the running server: {tools}
tools in {domains} domains, and {prompts} worked research prompts.

Other resources: `intel://guide/source-health` (which sources are
failing, stale or missing keys right now) and `intel://guide/measures`
(what the numbers mean and how they mislead).

## How to ask a strong question

- Name the period: "the last 30 days against the 30 days before", not
  "recently".
- Name the comparison: an earlier period, another place, or a stated
  baseline.
- Name the measure: event count or fatalities, price level or percentage
  change, people displaced at year end or arrivals during the year.
- Name the place: a country (many tools take an ISO-3 code), a region, a
  bounding box, or a saved area of interest.

A question with all four can be answered from tool output. A question
with none of them invites a story.

## What an answer from this server contains

- Values as the sources published them. Most responses name their source
  and carry a fetch timestamp; the date a value describes is often earlier
  than the fetch, so give both. Some tools return no observation date at
  all; say so rather than using the fetch time.
- Failures, sometimes. Some tools return `error`, `degraded` or
  `data_gaps` when a source is down or not configured. Many do not: when
  every upstream request fails they return an empty list, a zero count, a
  neutral score, a LOW risk label, an all-clear status or a false flag,
  with no marker. Read an empty list or a zero count as nothing returned,
  not nothing happened, and confirm with a second tool before calling a
  place quiet. `failing_sources` in the source-health resource names the
  sources whose last call failed.
- Citations. Briefs and digests number their sources.
- Old copies, counted. When a live fetch fails and an older cached copy
  exists, that copy is served. Dictionary responses carry `_stale` and
  `_stale_age_seconds`, but tools that reshape a response do not always
  pass the marker through. `stale_serves` in the source-health resource
  counts every stale copy this process served, per source.

## What this server will not do

- Trade, place orders, or say what to buy or sell.
- Forecast prices, elections or wars. Escalation, instability, risk and
  composite scores are weighted summaries of current readings against
  stated baselines, not probabilities.
- Prove causation. Series that move together, or one shortly after the
  other, may share a cause or be coincidence.
- Show history it did not record. Collected history (semantic search,
  timelines, baselines, area change detection) covers only the time the
  collector or server was running and storing. The exception is
  intel_history_backfill, which loads FRED and ECB publisher history
  into the history store for intel_series_history, intel_revisions and
  intel_day_timeline. Those values are the publisher's current vintage,
  so revisions made before the backfill do not show.
- Use keyed sources without their keys. Tools marked [needs ...] in the
  list below return an error naming the variable when it is not set; a
  few others fall back to a keyless source with less detail.
  `without_key` in the source-health resource says which, and whether
  each variable is set.
- See what its sources do not publish. Aircraft without a broadcast
  position, unlisted outlets, and regions outside a feed's coverage are
  absent, which is not the same as quiet.
- Confirm identities. A sanctions or entity name match is a text match.
measures:
# Measures glossary

What the numbers returned by this server's tools mean, and the mistakes
they invite.

## Amount outstanding versus flow

An amount outstanding (a stock) is a level at one moment: people
displaced at the end of a year, a central bank's balance sheet, money
supply. A flow is what happened during a period: arrivals during a year,
fund inflows in a week, fatalities in a month. Never add a stock to a
flow. A change in a stock is a net figure: a displaced population that
grew by 100,000 may have had 300,000 arrivals and 200,000 returns.

## Growth versus acceleration

Growth is how fast a level changes (prices 3 percent higher than a year
earlier). Acceleration is how fast the growth rate itself changes
(growth up from 2 to 3 percent). Slower growth is still growth: inflation
falling from 4 to 3 percent means prices are still rising, only more
slowly.

## Percent versus percentage points

A rate that moves from 4 percent to 5 percent rose by 1 percentage
point, which is a 25 percent increase in the rate itself. Yields,
spreads, policy rates and shares are compared in points; one point is
100 basis points.

## Seasonally adjusted

Many series repeat a calendar pattern: holiday spending, winter heating,
summer travel. A seasonally adjusted series has the expected pattern
removed, so one month can be compared with the month before. An
unadjusted series should be compared with the same period a year
earlier. Never compare an adjusted figure with an unadjusted one; check
which a series is before comparing.

## Observation, publication and collection dates

- Observation date: the period a value describes (March unemployment,
  the day an event took place).
- Publication date: when the publisher released it, often weeks after
  the observation, with revisions later still.
- Collection date: when this server fetched or saved it.

A value fetched today can describe last month or last year; annual
datasets such as World Bank indicators often trail by a year or more.
Report the observation date. The fetch time only tells you how fresh the
copy is. Some tools return no observation date; say so.

## Revisions

First releases are estimates. Economic series, event datasets and
displacement figures are revised after publication, sometimes by more
than the change being discussed. Say which release you used.

## Correlation and timing offsets

Two series that move together, or where one tends to move a few days
before the other, may share a cause, may be linked in either direction,
or may be coincidence. Coincidence becomes likely when many pairs or
many offsets are tried and only the best is reported. A lead or lag found
in one sample describes that sample. None of this shows that one thing
caused the other.

## Composite scores

Escalation, instability, risk, macro composite and stress scores are
weighted combinations of current inputs against stated baselines. They
summarize their inputs and are not probabilities. Some add a fixed amount
from a static country table: the instability index's `ucdp_floor` and
`displacement_boost` come from a baseline risk table, not from current
data, so a floor score says nothing about this week. Report the
components with the score; a null component was not measured.

## Missing data is not zero

Many tools report a source that failed, is not configured, or does not
cover a place with an error, a note or a `data_gaps` entry. That means
unknown, not none. Many tools do not: when every upstream request fails
they return an empty list, a zero count, a neutral score, a LOW risk
label, an all-clear status or a false flag, so an empty list or a zero
means nothing was returned, not that nothing happened. Zero events from a fetch that worked, in a region the source
covers and for a query that matched the place, is a measurement; zero
events in a region it does not cover is nothing at all.

keyedSources.without_key: ACLED event, unrest and risk tools return an error naming the missing credentials, and so does intel_instability_index without a country_code. With a country_code the index still scores, without its unrest and conflict inputs, and lists acled_unconfigured in data_gaps. When both are set but the sign-in request fails, the error says ACLED sign-in failed instead (reason acled_auth_failed).
intel_ucdp_events still sends the request; the API refuses it, and the tool returns an error with reason ucdp_unconfigured.
Energy prices, residential natural gas and electricity rates return an error.

intel_fred_series returns an error; the yield curve falls back to four Yahoo maturities with no 2s10s spread and no observation dates; central bank rates come only from a hand-kept table dated 2024-11 to 2025-02.
Internet outages fall back to the IODA public API.
Requests are anonymous, with OpenSky's lower anonymous limits.
Traffic flow and incident tools return an error.

healthScope: circuit_breakers covers requests made by this server process since it started; the collector, dashboard and CLI keep their own. An empty map means no requests yet, not that every source is healthy.

failing_sources lists every source whose last call from this process failed, whether or not its breaker has opened. In circuit_breakers, failures is the count of failed calls since the last success (0 after a success), and a breaker opens only after several failures in a row; total_successes and total_failures count every call since the process started.
stale_serves counts, per source, the stale cached copies this process served when a live fetch failed, whatever the payload type.

cache_freshness reads the cache database: the newest entry per key prefix, written by whichever process fetched it. A fresh entry shows a recent successful fetch, not that the collector is on schedule.

cache.requested_path is the database this process was configured to use; when it could not be opened, cache.fell_back is true and db_path is a temporary database that no other process shares. cache.available is false when the database could not be read at all. cache.moved is true when the file at db_path is gone, or is not the file this process first read, while this process still holds the old one open: its numbers then come from a file no other process shares. A file replaced before this resource was first read is not detected.
keyed_sources says whether each variable is set in this server's environment. It never shows values and does not check that a key works.
Not read here: vector store statistics (intel_vector_stats) and the collector's run history (intel_collection_health). Reading this resource starts no fetches.
